biggest_gap.title: Gate gap: no permission gate changes only a schedule's parameters, so a broken parameter comparison would let a user without the kind's run permission change what a schedule runs
biggest_gap.detail: PUT /api/jobs/schedules/{id} must refuse a change to the parameters from a user who lacks the kind's run permission. The real product does refuse it (403). But the only gate that sends a parameter change, step 2 of JobsWriteSetTests.A_user_who_may_only_add_schedules_cannot_schedule_a_kind_whose_run_permission_they_lack, also changes the cron (30 3 to 45 4, because steps 0 and 1 were refused). That request is refused for the cron alone. Round 6's new SameJson comparison is therefore never tested on its own as a security check. The new test with nested parameters only checks unchanged parameters (expects 200). Plant P7 made SameJson return true for any two numbers, and every gate and module test still passed. A user with only jobs.schedules.update could then change a self-check's steps from 3 to 12. For a cleanup-like kind with its own run permission, the same fault would let them change a retention number. The fix: in JobsWriteSetTests, add a PUT for a non-holder that keeps scheduleName, cron and isEnabled as stored and changes only (a) a number, (b) a nested string and (c) one key added or dropped, each expecting 403 jobs.typeNotAllowed, and check the stored payload is unchanged.
biggest_gap.evidence: plants/plantA-L4-L6-P7.diff (the P7 hunk in ScheduleEndpoints.SameJson: 'case JsonValueKind.Number: return true;'). plants/plantA-gates.log shows all 5 JobsWriteSetTests and all G2PermissionTests passed. plants/plantB-jobs-module-all.log shows 71 of 72 Jobs module tests passed, the one failure being the L4 plant's test. plants/CriticProofR6.cs failed on the plant with 'steps 3 -> 12 by a user without jobs.jobs.run: got 200'. attack/schedule-update-probe.txt shows the unplanted product answers 403 to the same change.

other_findings: 1. The builder's comparison driver and the documented path ('type the job name, Enter opens the best match', docs/decisions/p12-jobs-audit-labels-and-round-6.md) still fail at bar volume, for the fourth judged round (r2, r3, r5, r6). The decision record blames the seeder, but that was not the cause. GET /api/jobs/jobs?search=Self-check%20of%20the%20job%20queue returns total 24,628 with ranked:false, so the list framework's Enter focuses the grid and opens nothing.
